### Pro plan

The pro plan is where most production apps start. At $25 per month per organization, it delivers meaningfully higher usage limits, daily backups, and email support - the baseline for serious workloads.

## FAQ

### Is Supabase really free? [...] October 5, 2026

Supabase Pro is “from $25/month”. The word doing the work in that sentence is “from”. I went through the pricing page and the cost-control docs line by line on 5 October 2026 to work out what a real project pays, where the bill grows, and when it is worth leaving. Short version: one small project really is $25. Three projects is $45 before a single user shows up. And the spend cap protects you from less than most people assume.

results.title: Supabase Pricing Page and Costs Explained (2026)
results.snippet:
### Pro

Pro is Supabase's most popular pricing plan. It is the main starting point for companies building production applications.

Image

Source: Supabase.com

At $25/month, the Pro plan supports up to 100,000 monthly active users. It also includes a larger database size (8 GB per project), more storage (100 GB), higher bandwidth consumption (250 GB egress), and daily backups for seven days. Plus, it unlocks email support. [...] Supabase is not costly for small teams or early-stage startups. The Free tier offers generous limits, while the Pro plan starts at $25/month. Costs only increase when your app uses more compute, storage, bandwidth, monthly active users, or paid add-ons.

### Is Supabase cheaper than AWS?

Supabase can be cheaper and easier to budget than AWS because it offers predictable pricing plans. AWS may provide more services, but pricing can be harder to predict across multiple products. [...] Supabase is a masterclass in predictable pricing by using tiered plans, transparent overage policies, cost control, linked docs, and detailed FAQs.
 It offers four pricing plans: Free for basic projects, Pro ($25/month) for production apps, Team ($599/month) for scaling companies, and Enterprise for large organizations with custom needs.

Supabase Pro costs $25/month and bundles far more than just a database: Auth (50,000 MAU included), Storage (100 GB included), Edge Functions (2M invocations included), Realtime (200 concurrent connections included), and the Postgres database with Row Level Security. This is a Backend-as-a-Service platform, not a pure database — comparing it against database-only providers requires accounting for the additional services you would otherwise pay for separately. [...] Database pricing is highly variable. Costs depend on query patterns, connection pooling, IOPS, backup retention, and plan-specific limits that this calculator cannot fully model. Treat these as order-of-magnitude estimates and verify against each provider's pricing page and your actual usage.

### Scaling limits and user caps [...] Yes, Supabase has a free tier at no cost, with 500MB of database space, 5GB of egress and 50,000 monthly active users. It suits prototyping, but projects pause after 7 days of inactivity. Production apps need the Pro plan, which starts at $25 per month and removes the inactivity pause. [...] 50,000 monthly active users is the cap for the Free plan, so a viral launch can hit the plan's limits if the account is not upgraded.

Moving to the Pro plan at $25 per month increases this limit to 100,000 users, so scaling your application becomes significantly more affordable as your user base grows. At the Team tier, starting at $599 per month, the pricing model shifts entirely toward usage-based billing.
